title.zh: 卷一百七十八 列傳第六十五: 梁曾 劉敏中 王約 王結 宋衜 張伯淳
title.en: Volume 178 Biographies 65: Liang Ceng, Liu Minzhong, Wang Yue, Wang Jie, Song Dao, Zhang Bochun
title.raw: 卷一百七十八 列傳第六十五: 梁曾 劉敏中 王約 王結 宋衜 張伯淳 Volume 178 Biographies 65: Liang Ceng, Liu Minzhong, Wang Yue, Wang Jie, Song Dao, Zhang Bochun

sentences.zh: 梁曾，字貢父，燕人。

translations.literal: Liang Ceng, styled Gongfu, was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ceng, whose courtesy name was Gongfu, came from the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 祖守正，父德，皆以曾貴，贈安定郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouzheng and his father De, both because of Ceng's eminence, were posthumously enfeoffed as Dukes of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Ceng's prominence, both his grandfather Shouzheng and his father De were posthumously ennobled as Dukes of Anding.

sentences.zh: 曾少好學，日記書數千言。

translations.literal: Ceng from youth loved learning; each day he could memorize several thousand characters in writing.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Ceng loved study and could commit several thousand characters to memory each day.

sentences.zh: 中統四年，以翰林學士承旨王鶚薦，辟中書左三部令史，三轉為中書省掾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong, on the recommendation of Hanlin Academician Grand Preceptor Wang E, he was summoned as a clerk of the Left Three Departments of the Central Secretariat, and after three promotions became a secretary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 4 (1263), on the recommendation of Wang E, Grand Preceptor of the Hanlin Academy, he was appointed clerk of the Secretariat's left three departments and, after three promotions, rose to secretary in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，用累考及格，授雲南諸路行省都事，佩銀符。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan, through accumulated examinations passing the standard, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat for All Circuits, wearing a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 10 (1273), having passed the cumulative examinations, he was made chief administrator of the Yunnan regional secretariat and granted a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 久之，升員外郎。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 十五年，轉同知廣南西道左右兩江宣撫司事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to serve as Associate Commissioner of the Pacification Commission for the Left and Right Two Rivers of Western Guangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was transferred to associate commissioner of the pacification commission for the left and right two rivers of western Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 明年，除知南陽府。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed Prefect of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed prefect of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 唐、鄧二屬州為襄陽府所奪，曾按圖經、稽國製以聞，事得復舊。

translations.literal: The two subordinate prefectures Tang and Deng had been seized by Xiangyang Prefecture; Ceng consulted the gazetteers and examined the national regulations, reported the matter, and the former arrangement was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate prefectures of Tang and Deng had been absorbed by Xiangyang; Ceng checked the gazetteers and national regulations, reported the case, and jurisdiction was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 南陽在宋末為邊鄙，桑柘未成，而歲賦絲，民甚苦之，曾請折輸布，民便之。

translations.literal: Nanyang at the end of the Song had been a frontier region; mulberry and catalpa were not yet established, yet the annual levy was in silk, and the people suffered greatly; Ceng requested conversion of the tribute to cloth, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Song Nanyang had been a border district where mulberry groves were not yet established, yet the annual tax was levied in silk, which greatly burdened the people; Ceng petitioned to substitute cloth, to their relief.

sentences.zh: 十七年，朝廷以安南世子陳日烜不就徵，選曾使其國。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the Annamese heir Chen Rixuan did not respond to the summons, the court selected Ceng to go on a mission to that country.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, because the Annamese crown prince Chen Rixuan had not obeyed the imperial summons, the court chose Ceng to serve as envoy to Annam.

sentences.zh: 召見，賜三珠金虎符、貂裘一襲，進兵部尚書，與禮部尚書柴椿偕行。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience, granted a three-pearl gold tiger tally and one sable fur robe, promoted to Minister of War, and traveled together with Minister of Rites Chai Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he received a three-pearl gold tiger tally and a sable robe, was promoted to Minister of War, and set out with Minister of Rites Chai Chun.

sentences.zh: 至安南，語秘不傳。

translations.literal: On reaching Annam, his words were secret and not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: What was said in Annam was kept confidential and not recorded.

sentences.zh: 明年，日烜遣其叔遺愛，奉表從曾入獻方物。

translations.literal: The following year Rixuan sent his uncle Yi'ai, presenting a memorial and following Ceng to enter court and offer tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Rixuan sent his uncle Yi'ai, who presented a memorial and accompanied Ceng to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝封遺愛為安南國王，賜幣帛，遣歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor enfeoffed Yi'ai as King of Annam, bestowed silks and fabrics, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed Yi'ai as king of Annam, granted silks and fabrics, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，除曾湖南宣慰司副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Ceng was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Hunan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 Ceng was appointed vice commissioner of the Hunan pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 居三年，以疾去。

translations.literal: After three years in office he left on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，改淮西宣慰司副使，復以親老辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Huai-West Pacification Commission, but again declined on grounds of aged parents.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Huai-West pacification commission but again declined, citing his elderly parents.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，入見內殿，有旨令曾再使安南，授吏部尚書，賜三珠金虎符、襲衣、乘馬、弓矢、器幣，以禮部郎中陳孚為副。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, he entered audience in the inner hall; an edict ordered Ceng to go again on mission to Annam, appointed him Minister of Personnel, granted a three-pearl gold tiger tally, court robes, riding horses, bow and arrows, and ritual vessels, with Bureau Director of Rites Chen Fu as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he was received in the inner palace and ordered to return to Annam; he was made Minister of Personnel and given a three-pearl gold tiger tally, court dress, horses, bow and arrows, and ritual gifts, with Chen Fu of the Ministry of Rites as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 十二月，改授淮安路總管而行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was reassigned as Route Administrator of Huai'an and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was reassigned as route administrator of Huai'an and set out on the mission.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，至安南。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year he reached Annam.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 30 he arrived in Annam.

sentences.zh: 其國有三門：中曰陽明，左曰日新，右曰雲會，陪臣郊迎，將由日新門入。

translations.literal: That country had three gates: the center was called Yangming, the left Rixin, the right Yunhui; accompanying officials met him in the suburbs and intended to have him enter by the Rixin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had three gates—the central Yangming, the left Rixin, and the right Yunhui—and courtiers met him in the suburbs intending to bring him in through Rixin.

sentences.zh: 曾大怒曰：「奉詔不由中門，是我辱君命也。」

translations.literal: Ceng said in great anger: "To bear the imperial mandate and not enter by the central gate—this would be my disgracing the ruler's command."
translations.idiomatic: Ceng said angrily, "To carry an imperial mandate and not enter by the central gate would be to disgrace my sovereign's command."

sentences.zh: 即回館，既而請開雲會門入，曾复執不可，始自陽明門迎詔入。

translations.literal: He at once returned to the lodge; later they asked to open the Yunhui Gate for entry, but Ceng again held firm and would not agree, until at last they welcomed the edict in through the Yangming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the lodge at once; when they later asked to admit him through Yunhui, he again refused, and only then did they receive the edict through Yangming.

sentences.zh: 又責日燇親出迎詔，且講新朝尚右之禮。

translations.literal: He further charged Chen Rideng to come out in person to welcome the edict, and explained the new dynasty's rites honoring the right.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that Chen Rideng come out in person to receive the edict and explained the new court's protocol of honoring the right.

sentences.zh: 以書往復者三次，具宣布天子威德，而風其君入朝。

translations.literal: Letters were exchanged three times; he fully proclaimed the Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue, and urged their ruler to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds of letters passed between them as he proclaimed the emperor's majesty and urged their ruler to attend court.

sentences.zh: 世子陳日燇大感服，三月，令其國相陶子奇等從曾詣闕請罪，並上萬壽頌、金冊表章、方物，而以黃金器幣奇物遺曾為贐，曾不受，以還諸陶子奇。

translations.literal: The heir Chen Rideng was deeply moved and submitted; in the third month he ordered his Chancellor Tao Ziqi and others to follow Ceng to the court to beg pardon, and presented a longevity hymn, golden book memorial, and tribute goods, while sending Ceng golden vessels, coins, and rare objects as parting gifts; Ceng did not accept them and returned them to Tao Ziqi.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Chen Rideng was deeply impressed; in the third month he sent his chancellor Tao Ziqi and others with Ceng to court to plead guilty, presenting a longevity hymn, a golden-book memorial, and tribute, and also offered Ceng gold vessels, currency, and curios as farewell gifts, which Ceng refused and returned to Tao Ziqi.

sentences.zh: 八月，還京師，入見，進所與陳日燇往復議事書。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he returned to the capital, entered audience, and presented the letters exchanged with Chen Rideng on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned to the capital, was received in audience, and submitted the correspondence exchanged with Chen Rideng.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，解衣賜之，且令坐地上，右丞阿里意不然，帝怒曰：「梁曾兩使外國，以口舌息兵戈，爾何敢爾！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, removed his own garment to bestow it, and moreover ordered him to sit on the ground; Right Chancellor Ari was displeased, and the Emperor said in anger: "Liang Ceng has twice been envoy abroad and with words alone stilled arms—how dare you!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave him his own robe, and had him sit on the floor; Right Chancellor Ari objected, and the emperor said angrily, "Liang Ceng has twice gone abroad and stilled war with words alone—how dare you!"

sentences.zh: 是日，有親王至自和林，帝命酌酒，先賜曾，謂親王曰：「汝所辦者汝事，梁曾所辦，吾與汝之事，汝勿以為後也。」

translations.literal: That day a prince arrived from Karakorum; the Emperor ordered wine poured and first granted it to Ceng, saying to the prince: "What you have accomplished is your affair; what Liang Ceng has accomplished is my affair with you—do not take precedence."
translations.idiomatic: That day a prince arrived from Karakorum; the emperor ordered wine and gave it first to Ceng, telling the prince, "What you have done is your business; what Liang Ceng has done is my business with you—do not rank yourself ahead of him."

sentences.zh: 復於便殿賜酒饌，留宿禁中，語安南事，至二鼓方出。

translations.literal: Again in the side hall he was granted wine and food, kept overnight within the palace precincts, and discussed Annam affairs until the second watch before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: He was again feasted in the side hall, lodged overnight in the palace, and talked of Annam until the second watch before he left.

sentences.zh: 明日，陶子奇等見詔，陳其方物象、鸚鵡於庭，而命曾引所獻象。

translations.literal: The next day Tao Ziqi and others were received in audience with the edict; their tribute goods, elephants, and parrots were displayed in the courtyard, and the Emperor ordered Ceng to lead the presented elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tao Ziqi and others were received; their tribute, elephants, and parrots were shown in the courtyard, and the emperor ordered Ceng to lead the elephants they had presented.

sentences.zh: 曾以袖引之，象隨曾轉，如素馴者，復命引他像，亦然。

translations.literal: Ceng led them by his sleeve; the elephants turned as Ceng turned, as if long trained; ordered again to lead other elephants, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng led them by his sleeve, and the elephants turned with him as if long trained; when told to lead the others, they did the same.

sentences.zh: 帝以曾為福人，且問曰：「汝亦懼否？」

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Ceng a man of good fortune, and moreover asked: "Were you also afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Ceng for a man of good fortune and asked, "Were you afraid as well?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「雖懼，君命不敢違。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Though afraid, I did not dare disobey my ruler's command."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I was afraid, but I did not dare disobey my sovereign's command."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 或讒曾受安南賂者，帝以問曾，曾對曰：「安南以黃金器幣奇物遺臣，臣不受，以屬陶子奇矣。」

translations.literal: Some slandered Ceng for having received bribes from Annam; the Emperor questioned Ceng, and Ceng replied: "Annam sent me golden vessels, coins, and rare objects; I did not accept them and turned them over to Tao Ziqi."
translations.idiomatic: Some accused Ceng of taking bribes from Annam; when the emperor asked him, Ceng said, "Annam gave me gold vessels, currency, and curios; I refused them and returned them to Tao Ziqi."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「苟受之，何不可也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If you had accepted them, what would be wrong with that!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you had accepted them, what harm would there be!"

sentences.zh: 尋賜白金一錠、金幣二；

translations.literal: Shortly he was granted one ingot of white gold and two gold coins;
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given one ingot of white gold and two gold coins;

sentences.zh: 敕中書以使安南三珠金虎符與之。

translations.literal: an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to give him the three-pearl gold tiger tally used for missions to Annam.
translations.idiomatic: and the Secretariat was ordered to confer on him the three-pearl gold tiger tally for missions to Annam.

sentences.zh: 仍乘傳之任淮安。

translations.literal: He still traveled by relay post to take up his post at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He still traveled by relay post to take up office at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 到官，興學校，厲風俗，河南行省事有疑者，皆委曾議之。

translations.literal: On reaching office he established schools and encouraged customs; whenever the Henan Branch Secretariat had doubtful matters, all were entrusted to Ceng for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In office he promoted schools and improved local customs; whenever the Henan regional secretariat had doubtful matters, they were all referred to Ceng.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，除杭州路總管，戶口復者五萬二千四百戶，請禁莫夜鞫囚、游街、酷刑，朝廷是之，著為令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was appointed Prefect of Hangzhou Circuit; households restored numbered fifty-two thousand four hundred; he requested prohibition of nighttime interrogation, parading prisoners in the streets, and cruel punishments—the court approved and wrote it into statute.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1 (1297) he was appointed prefect of Hangzhou Circuit; fifty-two thousand four hundred households were restored; he petitioned to ban nighttime interrogation, parading prisoners, and cruel punishments, and the court approved and made it statute.

sentences.zh: 四年，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 先是，丁憂之制未行，曾上言請如禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, the mourning-leave system had not been in force; Ceng had memorialized requesting it follow ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the mourning-leave system had not been enforced; Ceng had memorialized that it should follow ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 七年，除潭州路總管，以未終制，不赴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Prefect of Tanzhou Circuit but, as mourning was not yet complete, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou Circuit but, as mourning was not yet complete, did not take office.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷兩浙都轉運鹽使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Director of Salt Transport for the Two Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to director of salt transport for the Two Zhe regions.

sentences.zh: 又明年，拜雲南行省參知政事，賜三珠金虎符。

translations.literal: The year after that he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat and granted a three-pearl gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was made vice administrator of the Yunnan regional secretariat and granted a three-pearl gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 尋召還京，辭以母喪未葬，扶柩北歸，至長蘆，有旨賜鈔一百錠，使營葬。

translations.literal: Soon summoned back to the capital, he declined on grounds that his mother's funeral was not yet completed; bearing the coffin north, at Changlu an edict granted one hundred ingots of paper money for burial arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned back to the capital, he declined because his mother's funeral was not yet complete; bearing the coffin north, at Changlu an edict granted one hundred ingots of paper money for the burial.

sentences.zh: 十年，召為中書參議，嘗預燕，賜只孫一襲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned as Participating Secretary of the Central Secretariat; he once attended a banquet and was granted one jisun robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was summoned as participating secretary of the Central Secretariat; he once attended a banquet and was granted one jisun robe.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉正奉大夫，出為河南行省參知政事，尋遷湖廣行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Grand Master of Positive Tribute, sent out as Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and soon transferred to Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to grand master of positive tribute, sent out as vice administrator of the Henan regional secretariat, and soon transferred to vice administrator of the Huguang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，以疾辭歸，敕賜藥物，存問備至。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhida he resigned and returned home due to illness; an edict granted medicines with the utmost solicitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 4 (1311) he resigned and returned home due to illness; an edict granted medicines with the utmost solicitude.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，仁宗以曾前朝舊臣，特授昭文館大學士、資德大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing, Emperor Renzong, because Ceng was an old minister of the previous reign, specially appointed him Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Grand Master of Virtuous Merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 (1312), Emperor Renzong, treating Ceng as a veteran of the prior reign, specially made him Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Grand Master of Virtuous Merit.

sentences.zh: 累章乞致仕，不允，復起為集賢侍講學士。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, but was not permitted; he was again raised to Attending Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire but was refused and was recalled as Attending Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 國有大政，必命曾與諸老議之。

translations.literal: Whenever the state had great affairs of government, Ceng was always ordered to deliberate with the elder statesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state faced major policy, Ceng was always summoned to consult with the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，奉詔代祀中岳等神。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he received an edict to perform sacrifice by proxy to the Central Peak and other deities.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 (1314) he was ordered to perform proxy sacrifices to the Central Peak and other spirits.

sentences.zh: 還至汴梁，以病不復職，寓居淮南，杜門不通賓客，惟日以書史自娛。

translations.literal: On returning to Bianliang he did not resume office because of illness, lodged in Huainan, shut his door and did not receive guests, and each day took pleasure only in books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Bianliang, he did not resume office because of illness, lived in Huainan, shut his door to visitors, and passed his days only with books and histories.

sentences.zh: 至治二年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhizhi 2 (1322) at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 卒之前十日，有大星隕於所居，流光燭​​地，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Ten days before his death a great star fell at his residence; its flowing light illuminated the ground, and all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days before his death a great star fell at his dwelling; its light lit the ground, and everyone took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: ○劉敏中

translations.literal: ○ Liu Minzhong
translations.idiomatic: ○ Liu Minzhong

sentences.zh: 劉敏中，字端甫，濟南章丘人。

translations.literal: Liu Minzhong, styled Duanfu, was a man of Zhangqiu in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Minzhong, whose courtesy name was Duanfu, came from Zhangqiu in Jinan.

sentences.zh: 幼卓異不凡，年十三，語其父景石曰：「昔賢足於學而不求知，豐於功而不自炫，此後人所弗逮也。」

translations.literal: From youth he was outstanding and not ordinary; at thirteen he said to his father Jingshi: "The sages of old were sufficient in learning yet did not seek to display knowledge, abundant in achievement yet did not boast of themselves—this is what later men cannot match."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was remarkably gifted; at thirteen he told his father Jingshi, "The sages of old were learned enough not to parade their knowledge and accomplished enough not to boast—later men cannot match that."

sentences.zh: 父奇之。

translations.literal: His father marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: His father was astonished.

sentences.zh: 鄉先生杜仁傑愛其文，亟稱之。

translations.literal: The village elder Du Renjie loved his writings and repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The local scholar Du Renjie admired his writing and praised him often.

sentences.zh: 敏中嘗與同儕各言其志，曰：「自幼至老，相見而無愧色，乃吾志也。」

translations.literal: Minzhong once spoke with his peers, each stating his ambition, and said: "From youth to old age, to meet one another without a blush of shame—that is my ambition."
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he and his companions each stated their ambitions, Minzhong said, "My ambition is to meet others from youth to old age without shame."

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，由中書掾擢兵部主事，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, from Secretariat secretary he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of War, and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 11 (1274) he rose from Secretariat secretary to director in the Ministry of War and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 權臣桑哥秉政，敏中劾其奸邪，不報，遂辭職歸其鄉。

translations.literal: The powerful minister Sangge held government; Minzhong impeached his treachery and wickedness, received no response, and then resigned and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the powerful minister Sangge dominated the government, Minzhong impeached him for corruption; when nothing came of it, he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 既而起為御史臺都事。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised again as Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled as director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時同官王約以言去，敏中杜門稱疾。

translations.literal: At that time his colleague Wang Yue had left office because of his words; Minzhong shut his door and claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his colleague Wang Yue had been driven out for speaking up; Minzhong shut his door and pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 台臣請視事，敏中曰：「使約無罪而被劾，吾固不當出；

translations.literal: Censorate colleagues asked him to resume duties; Minzhong said: "If Yue were without guilt yet impeached, I certainly should not come out;
translations.idiomatic: When censorate colleagues urged him to return to duty, Minzhong said, "If Yue was innocent yet impeached, I certainly should not appear;

sentences.zh: 誠有罪耶，則我既為同僚，又為交友，不能諫止，亦不無過也。」

translations.literal: if he truly had guilt, then I, being both his colleague and his friend, could not remonstrate and stop it—nor am I without fault."
translations.idiomatic: if he was guilty, then as both his colleague and his friend I failed to stop him and am not without fault either."

sentences.zh: 出為燕南肅政廉訪副使，入為國子司業，遷翰林直學士，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He went out as Vice Commissioner of the Yan-South Office for Scrutinizing Governance and Integrity, entered as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, was transferred to Hanlin Direct Academician, and concurrently served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as vice commissioner of the Yan-South integrity commission, recalled as vice director of the Directorate of Education, promoted to Hanlin direct academician, and also made chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，詔遣宣撫使巡行諸道，敏中出使遼東、山北諸郡，守令恃貴幸暴橫者，一繩以法；

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade an edict dispatched Pacification Commissioners to tour the circuits; Minzhong went on mission to the prefectures of Liaodong and Shanbei, and magistrates who relied on favor and committed violence and arrogance were all bound by law;
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 7 (1303) pacification commissioners were sent to tour the circuits; Minzhong toured Liaodong and Shanbei, and every magistrate who relied on patronage to act violently was prosecuted;

sentences.zh: 錦州雨水為災，輒發廩賑之。

translations.literal: at Jinzhou rain and flood became a disaster, and he at once opened the granaries to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: when rain and flood struck Jinzhou, he opened the granaries at once for relief.

sentences.zh: 除東平路總管，擢陝西行台治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Route Administrator of Dongping, then promoted to Attending Secretary and Investigating Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made route administrator of Dongping, then promoted to attending secretary and investigating censor on the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年，召為集賢學士，商議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was summoned as academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 上疏陳十事，曰整朝綱，省庶政，進善良，剔姦蠹，顯公道，杜私門，廣恩澤，實鈔法，嚴武備，舉封贈。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters: to rectify court discipline, reduce miscellaneous administration, advance the good and able, eliminate treacherous parasites, display public justice, block private factions, broaden grace and favor, make paper currency solid, tighten military preparedness, and promote posthumous enfeoffment and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized ten proposals: restore court discipline, streamline routine administration, promote the worthy, purge corruption, uphold public justice, shut private factions, extend imperial grace, stabilize paper currency, strengthen defenses, and revive posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，奸臣希中旨，贊其邪謀，敏中援禮力爭之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzong died, treacherous ministers curried favor with the central intent and supported their wicked plot; Minzhong cited ritual and strove against it with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Chengzong died, scheming ministers courted the throne's wishes and backed a wicked plot; Minzhong cited ritual and fought it fiercely.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，召敏中至上京，庶政多所更定，授集賢學士、皇太子贊善，仍商議中書省事，賜金幣有加。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Minzhong was summoned to the Upper Capital; many routine policies were revised and settled; he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Tutor to the Heir Apparent, still deliberating on Central Secretariat affairs, with additional grants of gold and coins.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong acceded, Minzhong was called to the Upper Capital; many policies were revised; he was made academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and tutor to the heir apparent, still deliberating on Secretariat affairs, with extra gifts of gold and coins.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜河南行省參知政事，俄改治書侍御史，出為淮西肅政廉訪使，轉山東宣慰使，遂召為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, soon changed to Attending Secretary and Investigating Censor, sent out as Commissioner of the Huai-West Office for Scrutinizing Governance and Integrity, transferred to Shandong Pacification Commissioner, and then summoned as Hanlin Academician Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice administrator of the Henan regional secretariat, then attending secretary and investigating censor, then commissioner of the Huai-West integrity office, then Shandong pacification commissioner, and finally summoned as Hanlin grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿集議弭災之道，敏中疏列七事，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the dukes and ministers to assemble and discuss ways to quell calamities; Minzhong memorialized seven matters, and the Emperor praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered the ministers to discuss how to avert calamity, Minzhong listed seven measures, which the emperor praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 以疾還鄉里。

translations.literal: Because of illness he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 敏中平生，身不懷幣，口不論錢；

translations.literal: Throughout his life Minzhong did not carry coins on his person, nor did his mouth discuss money;
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Minzhong carried no money on his person and never spoke of wealth;

sentences.zh: 義不苟進，進必有所匡救，援據今古，雍容不迫。

translations.literal: in righteousness he would not advance casually; when he advanced he always had something to correct and save, citing past and present, easy and unhurried.
translations.idiomatic: he would not advance office without principle, and whenever he did advance he sought to remedy wrongs, citing past and present with calm assurance.

sentences.zh: 每以時事為憂，或鬱而弗伸，則戚形於色，中夜嘆息，至淚濕枕席。

translations.literal: He constantly took the affairs of the time as his worry; when frustrated and unable to express himself, sorrow showed in his countenance; in the middle of the night he would sigh, until tears wet pillow and mat.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly worried over public affairs; when thwarted, sorrow showed on his face, and at midnight he would sigh until his pillow was wet with tears.

sentences.zh: 為文辭，理備辭明，有《中庵集》二十五卷。

translations.literal: In literary composition his reasoning was complete and his wording clear; he had the Collected Works of the Central Hermitage in twenty-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were lucid and well reasoned; he left the Collected Works of the Central Hermitage in twenty-five juan.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanyou 5 (1318) at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫、柱國，追封齊國公，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, with the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, with the posthumous title Wénjiǎn (Cultured and Simple).

sentences.zh: ○王約

translations.literal: ○ Wang Yue
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wang Yue

sentences.zh: 王約，字彥博，其先汴人，祖通，北徙真定。

translations.literal: Wang Yue, styled Yanbo; his ancestors were men of Bian, and his grandfather Tong moved north to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, whose courtesy name was Yanbo, was descended from Bian; his grandfather Tong moved north to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 約性穎悟，風格不凡。

translations.literal: Yue by nature was quick and perceptive, his manner not ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was quick-witted and of uncommon bearing.

sentences.zh: 從中丞魏初遊，博覽經史，工文辭，務達國體，時好不以動其心。

translations.literal: He followed Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Chu in study, broadly read the classics and histories, was skilled in literary composition, strove to grasp the substance of state policy, and current fashions did not move his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Chu, read widely in the classics and histories, wrote well, and sought to grasp statecraft; fashionable tastes did not sway him.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，翰林學士王磐薦為從事，承旨火魯火孫以司徒開府，奏授從仕郎、翰林國史院編修官，兼司徒府掾。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, Hanlin Academician Wang Pan recommended him as an attendant; Grand Preceptor Huoluohuosun, opening a bureau as Minister of Works, memorialized to appoint him Attendant Gentleman and Compiler of the Hanlin National History Institute, concurrently secretary of the Minister of Works bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276), Hanlin academician Wang Pan recommended him; when Grand Preceptor Huoluohuosun opened the Minister of Works bureau, Yue was appointed attendant gentleman and compiler in the Hanlin National History Institute, also serving as secretary in that bureau.

sentences.zh: 既而辟掾中書，除禮部主事。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as secretary of the Central Secretariat and appointed Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recruited to the Secretariat and made director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜監察御史，授承務郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Investigating Censor and granted the rank of Gentleman for Court Service.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he was appointed investigating censor with the rank of gentleman for court service.

sentences.zh: 首請建儲及修史事。

translations.literal: He was the first to request establishing the heir and compiling the histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to petition for designating an heir and compiling the dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 時丞相桑哥銜參政郭佑為中丞時奏誅右丞盧世榮等，故誣以他罪，約上章直佑冤。

translations.literal: At that time Chancellor Sangge bore a grudge because Vice Administrator Guo You, when serving as Censor-in-Chief, had memorialized for the execution of Right Chancellor Lu Shirong and others; therefore he falsely charged other crimes; Yue submitted a memorial to vindicate You's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Sangge still resented Vice Administrator Guo You for having, as censor-in-chief, urged the execution of Right Chancellor Lu Shirong and others, and now framed him on other charges; Yue memorialized to clear Guo's name.

sentences.zh: 按治成都鹽運使王鼎不法，罷官除名。

translations.literal: He investigated and prosecuted Wang Ding, Salt Transport Commissioner of Chengdu, for unlawful conduct, removed him from office, and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted Wang Ding, salt transport commissioner of Chengdu, for misconduct, stripped him of office, and erased his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 轉御史臺都事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 南台侍御史程文海入言事，多斥桑哥罪。

translations.literal: Southern Branch Attending Censor Cheng Wenhai entered to speak on affairs, largely denouncing Sangge's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Branch attending censor Cheng Wenhai came to court and spoke at length against Sangge's crimes.

sentences.zh: 桑哥怒，又以約與之表裡，六奏殺之，上不從。

translations.literal: Sangge was angry, and because Yue was in league with him outwardly and inwardly, six times memorialized to have him killed; the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge was furious and, believing Yue was Cheng's ally, six times memorialized for his execution; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 約以隴西地遠，請立行台陝西，詔從之。

translations.literal: Yue, because Longxi territory was remote, requested establishing a branch secretariat in Shaanxi; an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: Because Longxi was remote, Yue petitioned to establish a Shaanxi branch secretariat, and the edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 出賑河間饑民，均核有方，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Sent out to relieve the famine victims of Hejian, he had effective methods of equal distribution and verification, and very many were wholly saved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to relieve famine in Hejian, he distributed relief fairly and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，遷中書右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat's right department.

sentences.zh: 四月，成宗即位，言二十二事，曰實京師，放差稅，開獵禁，蠲逋負，賑窮獨，停冗役，禁鷹房，振風憲，除宿蠹，慰遠方，卻貢獻，詢利病，利農民，勵學校，立義倉，核稅戶，重名爵，明賞罰，擇守令，汰官屬，定律令，革兩司。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Emperor Chengzong took the throne; he spoke of twenty-two matters, namely: to solidify the capital, release miscellaneous taxes, open hunting prohibitions, remit arrears, relieve the destitute and alone, halt redundant corvée, forbid the falconry offices, invigorate the wind of the censorate, remove long-standing parasites, comfort distant regions, reject excessive tribute, inquire into benefits and harms, benefit farmers, encourage schools, establish charity granaries, verify tax households, honor titles and ranks, clarify rewards and punishments, select prefects and magistrates, eliminate redundant subordinates, fix laws and ordinances, and reform the two departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when Emperor Chengzong acceded, he proposed twenty-two reforms: strengthen the capital, reduce miscellaneous taxes, ease hunting bans, remit arrears, aid the destitute, halt redundant labor, curb the falconry offices, invigorate the censorate, purge entrenched corruption, reassure distant regions, cut excessive tribute, inquire into public welfare, aid farmers, promote schools, establish charity granaries, verify tax households, honor titles, clarify rewards and punishments, choose capable local officials, trim redundant staff, codify laws, and reform the two secretariat departments.

sentences.zh: 又請中書去繁文，一取信於行省，一責成於六部。

translations.literal: He further requested that the Central Secretariat remove redundant documents, place reliance wholly on the branch secretariats in one respect, and hold the Six Ministries responsible in another.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked the Secretariat to cut red tape, rely on the regional secretariats for one class of matters, and hold the six ministries accountable for another.

sentences.zh: 調兵部郎中，改禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Director of the Ministry of War, then changed to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to bureau director in the Ministry of War, then made bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 請行贈諡之典以旌忠勳，付時政記於史館以備纂錄，立供需府以專供億，皆從而行之。

translations.literal: He requested instituting the rite of posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous titles to honor loyal merit, entrusting records of current policy to the History Institute for compilation, and establishing a Supply and Demand Office to specialize in provisions—all were followed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to revive posthumous honors for loyal service, to lodge current-policy records in the History Institute for compilation, and to establish a supply office for provisioning—all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林直學士、知制誥同修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Direct Academician, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and Concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin direct academician, drafter of imperial edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 奉詔賑京畿東道饑民，發米五十萬石，所活五十餘萬人。

translations.literal: By imperial edict he relieved famine victims of the eastern circuit of the capital region, issued five hundred thousand shi of grain, and those wholly saved alive numbered more than five hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he relieved famine in the eastern capital region, issued five hundred thousand shi of grain, and saved more than five hundred thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 因條疏京東利病十事，請發米續賑之，中書用其言，民獲以蘇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he itemized ten matters of benefit and harm in the eastern capital region, requesting grain be issued to continue relief; the Central Secretariat adopted his words, and the people were able to recover.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized ten measures concerning welfare and hardship in the eastern capital region and asked for more grain for relief; the Secretariat adopted his proposal, and the people recovered.

sentences.zh: 高麗王昛年老，傳國子謜，有不安其政者，飛讒離間，及謜朝京師，潛使人賂用事者，留謜不遣。

translations.literal: The King of Goryeo Wang Chon was old and had transferred the state to his son Wang Jeon; those discontented with his government sent slander flying to sow division, and when Jeon came to court at the capital, they secretly sent men to bribe those in power, keeping Jeon and not sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: King Wang Chon of Goryeo was elderly and had passed the throne to his son Wang Jeon; malcontents spread slander, and when Jeon came to the capital, they secretly bribed court officials to detain him.

sentences.zh: 昛復位，乃委用小人，厚斂淫刑，國人群訴於朝。

translations.literal: Chon resumed the throne and then entrusted petty men, levying heavily and imposing excessive punishments; the people of the state appealed in crowds to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Chon resumed rule he relied on petty men, imposed heavy taxes and harsh punishments, and the people appealed en masse to the court.

sentences.zh: 中書令執其首惡，系刑部，其黨復不悛，奏屬約驗問。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat ordered the arrest of the chief culprits and imprisoned them in the Ministry of Justice; their faction again would not repent, and it was memorialized that Yue should investigate and question them.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat arrested the ringleaders and held them in the Ministry of Justice; when their faction remained unrepentant, the court assigned Yue to investigate.

sentences.zh: 約至，宣布明詔，而諭之曰：「天地間至親者父子，至重者君臣。

translations.literal: When Yue arrived he proclaimed the clear edict and instructed them, saying: "Between Heaven and earth the closest bond is father and son, the weightiest relation is ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue arrived he proclaimed the imperial edict and told them, "Between heaven and earth nothing is closer than father and son, and nothing weightier than ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 彼小人知自利，寧肯為汝家國地耶！」

translations.literal: Those petty men know only self-profit—would they ever act for the sake of your house and state!"
translations.idiomatic: Those petty men care only for themselves—would they ever act for your house and kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 昛感泣，謝曰：「臣年耄，聽信憸邪，是以致此，今聞命矣。

translations.literal: Chon wept in emotion and apologized, saying: "Your subject is aged; I listened to the treacherous and wicked, and thus brought this about—now I have heard the command.
translations.idiomatic: Chon wept and said, "I am old; I listened to the wicked and brought this on myself—now I have heard your command.

sentences.zh: 願奉表自雪，且請子謜還國，其小人黨與，悉聽使者治。」

translations.literal: I wish to present a memorial to clear myself, and moreover request that my son Jeon return to the state; as for the petty men's faction, let the envoy deal with them entirely."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to submit a memorial to clear my name and ask that my son Jeon return home; let your envoy punish the faction of petty men as he sees fit."

sentences.zh: 翼日，約逮捕覆按其罪，流二十二人，杖三人，黜有官者二人。

translations.literal: The next day Yue arrested them, reviewed and pressed their crimes, exiled twenty-two men, caned three, and dismissed two who held office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yue arrested and tried them, exiling twenty-two, caning three, and dismissing two officials.

sentences.zh: 命故臣洪子籓為相，俾更弊政，罷非道水驛十三，免耽羅貢非土產物，東民大喜。

translations.literal: He appointed the former minister Hong Ja-bon as chancellor, had him reform corrupt policies, abolished thirteen improper water courier stations, exempted tribute from Tamna of non-native products, and the eastern people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the former minister Hong Ja-bon as chancellor to reform abuses, abolished thirteen improper courier stations, ended Tamna's tribute of non-native goods, and the eastern people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 還報，稱旨，除太常少卿。

translations.literal: On returning to report, his work accorded with the imperial intent, and he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His report pleased the throne, and he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋詔約同宗正、御史讞獄京師，約辭職在清廟，帝不允。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict ordered Yue, together with the Director of the Imperial Clan and censors, to judge cases in the capital prisons; Yue declined on grounds of duties at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, but the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered, with the director of the imperial clan and censors, to judge capital prison cases; Yue pleaded duties at the ancestral temple, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃閱諸獄，決二百六十六人，當死者七十二人，釋無罪者八十六人，平反吳得誠冤，嫁良家入倡女十人，杖流元旦帶刀闌入殿庭者八十人。

translations.literal: He then reviewed all the prisons, deciding two hundred sixty-six cases: seventy-two deserving death, eighty-six released as without guilt; he reversed the injustice of Wu Decheng, married off ten women of good families who had entered brothels, and caned or exiled eighty men who on New Year's Day had carried swords and forced their way into the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed all prisons and decided 266 cases: 72 condemned to death, 86 released as innocent; he cleared Wu Decheng's wrongful conviction, married off ten respectable women forced into brothels, and punished 80 men who had forced their way into the palace courtyard armed on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 因議鬥毆殺人者宜減死一等，著為令。

translations.literal: He then deliberated that those who killed in brawling should have death reduced by one degree, and this was written as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed reducing the death penalty by one degree for killings in brawls, and this was enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 又以浙民於行省、南台互訟不決，命約訊之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Zhejiang people had lawsuits between the branch secretariat and the Southern Branch Censorate that could not be decided, Yue was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang litigants could not obtain a ruling between the regional secretariat and the southern censorate, Yue was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 約至杭，二十日而理，省、台無異辭。

translations.literal: Yue reached Hangzhou and settled the cases in twenty days; neither the secretariat nor the censorate had differing words.
translations.idiomatic: Yue reached Hangzhou and settled the cases in twenty days to the satisfaction of both offices.

sentences.zh: 特拜刑部尚書，以錄前功。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Minister of Justice to record his prior merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Minister of Justice in recognition of his earlier service.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，仁宗至自懷州，肅清宮禁，以平章賽典赤、安西王阿難答與左丞相阿忽台潛謀為變，命刑曹按責其狀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, Emperor Renzong arrived from Huai Prefecture, purged the palace precincts, and because Grand Councillor Saidu, Prince of Anxi Ananda, and Left Chancellor Ahutai had secretly plotted rebellion, ordered the penal offices to investigate and press their cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 11 (1307), when Emperor Renzong arrived from Huai Prefecture and purged the palace, Grand Councillor Saidu, Prince of Anxi Ananda, and Left Chancellor Ahutai were found to have plotted rebellion, and the penal offices were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「在法，謀逆不必搒掠，竟當伏誅。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "By law, for plotting treason there is no need for beating and torture; in the end they should submit to execution."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "By law, treason need not be beaten into confession—they should simply be executed."

sentences.zh: 由是結知仁宗。

translations.literal: From this he formed a bond of trust with Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won Renzong's trust.

sentences.zh: 富寧庫失金，約疑番直宿衛者盜之，未幾，果得實，庫官吏獲免。

translations.literal: The Funing treasury lost gold; Yue suspected the rotating night guards of the palace guard had stolen it; before long the truth was indeed obtained, and the treasury officials were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Funing treasury lost gold, Yue suspected the rotating palace guards; the thief was soon found, and the treasury officials were cleared.

sentences.zh: 監察御史言通州倉米三萬石，因雨而濕。

translations.literal: An investigating censor reported that thirty thousand shi of grain in the Tongzhou granary had been dampened by rain.
translations.idiomatic: An investigating censor reported that 30,000 shi of grain in the Tongzhou granary had been ruined by rain.

sentences.zh: 約謂必積氣所蒸，驗且堪用，釋守者罪。

translations.literal: Yue said it must have been steam from accumulated vapor; on inspection it was still usable, and the keepers' guilt was released.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said it was only surface damp from stored heat; inspection showed the grain was still usable, and the keepers were cleared.

sentences.zh: 宗王兄弟二人守邊，兄陰有異志，弟諫不聽，即上馬馳去，兄遣奴挾弓矢追之，弟發矢斃其奴，兄訴囚其弟，獄當死。

translations.literal: Two princely brothers guarded the frontier; the elder secretly harbored a different intent; the younger remonstrated but was not heeded, and at once mounted and galloped away; the elder sent a slave with bow and arrows in pursuit; the younger shot an arrow and killed the slave; the elder complained and imprisoned his brother, and the case called for death.
translations.idiomatic: Two princely brothers guarded the frontier; the elder secretly plotted rebellion; when the younger remonstrated in vain and fled on horseback, the elder sent an armed slave in pursuit; the younger shot the slave dead; the elder had his brother imprisoned on a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 約慮囚曰：「兄之奴，即弟之奴，況殺之有故。」

translations.literal: Yue considered the prisoner and said: "The elder's slave is also the younger's slave, and moreover the killing had cause."
translations.idiomatic: Yue reviewed the case and said, "The elder's slave was also the younger's servant, and the killing was justified."

sentences.zh: 立釋之。

translations.literal: He at once released him.
translations.idiomatic: He released him at once.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，請定丁憂之制，申旌表之恩，免都城煤炭之徵，皆從之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites, requested fixing the regulations for mourning one's parents, renewed the grace of commendatory tablets, and exempted the capital from the coal levy—all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Minister of Rites, he petitioned to codify mourning regulations, revive commendatory honors, and abolish the capital coal tax—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 京民王氏，仕江南而歿，有遺腹子，其女育之，年十六，乃訴其姊匿貲若干，有司責之急。

translations.literal: A capital resident surnamed Wang had served in Jiangnan and died, leaving a posthumous son; his daughter reared him; at sixteen he sued his elder sister for concealing a certain amount of property, and the officials pressed the case urgently.
translations.idiomatic: A Wang family of the capital had served in Jiangnan and died, leaving a posthumous son whom his daughter raised; at sixteen the boy sued his elder sister for hiding property, and officials pressed the case hard.

sentences.zh: 約視其牘曰：「無父之子，育之成人，且不絕王氏祀，姊之恩居多。

translations.literal: Yue looked at the documents and said: "A son without a father, reared to adulthood, and the Wang sacrifices not cut off—the elder sister's kindness is the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Yue read the petition and said, "She raised a fatherless boy to manhood and preserved the Wang line—the elder sister's kindness outweighs all.

sentences.zh: 誠利其貲，寧育之至今日耶！」

translations.literal: If she truly coveted his property, would she have reared him until today!"
translations.idiomatic: If she had wanted his money, would she have raised him to this day?"

sentences.zh: 改前議而斥之。

translations.literal: He changed the prior decision and rebuked the plaintiff.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed the earlier ruling and dismissed the suit.

sentences.zh: 柴氏初無子，命張氏子後，既得己子，張出為僧，柴之子又歿，僧乃訟家產，詔約詰之。

translations.literal: The Chai family at first had no son and appointed a Zhang son as heir; after they obtained their own son, the Zhang heir left to become a monk; the Chai son also died; the monk then sued for the family property; an edict ordered Yue to question him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chai family, childless at first, adopted a Zhang heir; when they later had a son of their own, the Zhang heir became a monk; after the Chai son died the monk sued for the estate, and Yue was ordered to examine the case.

sentences.zh: 約問曰：「汝出家，既分承汝師衣缽，又何為得柴氏業乎？」

translations.literal: Yue asked: "You left home to become a monk and have already inherited your master's robe and bowl—why should you obtain the Chai family's estate?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue asked, "You left the world and inherited your master's lineage—why should you claim the Chai estate?"

sentences.zh: 僧不能答，遂歸柴氏應後者。

translations.literal: The monk could not answer and the property was returned to the one who should succeed the Chai line.
translations.idiomatic: The monk had no reply, and the property went to the rightful Chai heir.

sentences.zh: 至大二年正月，上武宗尊號及冊皇后，凡典禮儀注，約悉總之如製。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhida, when Emperor Wuzong's honorific title was elevated and the empress was installed, all ritual protocols and procedures Yue oversaw entirely according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhida 2 (1309), when Wuzong's honorific title was elevated and the empress installed, Yue directed all ritual protocols according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，雅知約名，思用以自輔，擢太子詹事丞。

translations.literal: When Renzong was in the Eastern Palace he had long known Yue's reputation and wished to use him as his own aide, promoting him to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was heir apparent he had long known Yue's reputation and wished him as an adviser, promoting him to vice director of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 從幸五台山，約諫不可久留，即日還上京。

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial tour to Mount Wutai, Yue remonstrated that they should not stay long, and that very day they returned to the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the tour to Mount Wutai, Yue urged that they not linger long, and they returned to the Upper Capital the same day.

sentences.zh: 初，安西王封於秦，既以謀逆誅，國除，版賦入詹事院。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Anxi had been enfeoffed in Qin; after he was executed for plotting treason the state was abolished and its tax registers entered the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Anxi had been enfeoffed in Qin; after his execution for treason the principality was abolished and its revenues went to the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 至是，大臣奏請封其子，復國。

translations.literal: At this time great ministers memorialized requesting to enfeoff his son and restore the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now ministers memorialized to enfeoff his son and restore the principality.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以問，約曰：「安西以何罪誅？

translations.literal: Renzong asked Yue about it; Yue said: "For what crime was Anxi executed?
translations.idiomatic: Renzong asked Yue, who said, "For what crime was the Prince of Anxi executed?

sentences.zh: 今復之，何以懲將來！」

translations.literal: To restore it now—how would that warn the future!"
translations.idiomatic: If we restore it now, how will we warn those who come after?"

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明年，進太子副詹事，約抗章諫節飲，辭意懇切，仁宗嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The following year he was advanced to Vice Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Yue submitted a memorial resisting excessive drinking, his words earnest and sincere, and Renzong praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made vice grand mentor of the heir; Yue memorialized against excessive drinking in earnest terms, and Renzong praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 承製立左衛率府，統侍衛軍萬人，同列欲署軍官，約持不可，眾難之曰：「東宮非樞密使耶？」

translations.literal: By imperial order the Left Guard Command was established to command ten thousand guardsmen; colleagues wished to sign military officers, but Yue held firm that it could not be done; the crowd objected, saying: "Is not the Eastern Palace the Bureau of Military Affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order the Left Guard Command was established with ten thousand guardsmen; colleagues wanted to appoint army officers, but Yue objected; they protested, "Is the Eastern Palace not the Bureau of Military Affairs?"

sentences.zh: 約曰：「詹事，東宮官也，預樞密事可乎？」

translations.literal: Yue said: "The Grand Mentor is an Eastern Palace office—how can it participate in Bureau of Military Affairs matters?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The grand mentor is an Eastern Palace office—how can it take on Bureau of Military Affairs duties?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗復召問約，對曰：「皇太子事，不敢不為；

translations.literal: Renzong again summoned and questioned Yue; he replied: "Matters of the Crown Prince—I dare not fail to act;
translations.idiomatic: Renzong questioned him again; Yue replied, "Matters of the crown prince I dare not neglect;

sentences.zh: 天子事，不敢為。」

translations.literal: matters of the Son of Heaven—I dare not act."
translations.idiomatic: matters of the Son of Heaven I dare not undertake."

sentences.zh: 仁宗悟，竟罷議。

translations.literal: Renzong understood and in the end dropped the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong understood and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 同列复傳命增立右衛率府，取河南蒙古軍萬人統之。

translations.literal: Colleagues again transmitted orders to add the Right Guard Command, taking ten thousand Mongol troops of Henan to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues again ordered establishment of a Right Guard Command with ten thousand Henan Mongol troops.

sentences.zh: 約屏人語曰：「左衛率府，舊制有之，今置右府何為？

translations.literal: Yue, screening others, spoke privately: "The Left Guard Command existed in the old system—why establish a right command now?
translations.idiomatic: Yue spoke privately: "The Left Guard Command is an old institution—why add a right command now?

sentences.zh: 諸公宜深思之，不可累儲宮也。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen ought to think deeply—one must not burden the Heir Apparent's palace."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen should think carefully—you must not burden the heir's establishment."

sentences.zh: 又命取安西兵器，給宿衛士。

translations.literal: They also ordered taking weapons from Anxi to supply the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: They also ordered weapons taken from Anxi for the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 約謂詹事完澤曰：「詹事移文數千里取兵器，人必驚疑。

translations.literal: Yue said to Grand Mentor Wanze: "The Grand Mentor's office sends documents thousands of li to fetch weapons—people will surely be alarmed and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yue told Grand Mentor Wanze, "If the heir's office sends orders thousands of li for weapons, people will be alarmed.

sentences.zh: 主上聞之，奈何？」

translations.literal: When the sovereign hears of it, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: What will the sovereign think when he hears of it?"

sentences.zh: 完澤色慚曰：「實慮不及此。」

translations.literal: Wanze flushed with shame and said: "I truly did not consider this."
translations.idiomatic: Wanze said abashed, "I truly had not thought of that."

sentences.zh: 又命福建取繡工童男女六人。

translations.literal: They also ordered Fujian to supply six boy and girl embroidery artisans.
translations.idiomatic: They also ordered six boy and girl embroidery artisans brought from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 約言曰：「福建去京師六七千里，使人父子兄弟相離，有司承風動擾，豈美事耶！」

translations.literal: Yue spoke, saying: "Fujian is six or seven thousand li from the capital—sending people would separate fathers, sons, and brothers; officials would take the wind and stir disturbance—how is this a fine affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Fujian is six or seven thousand li away—this would tear families apart and set officials stirring up trouble—how can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗止之，稱善再三。

translations.literal: Renzong stopped it and praised him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong stopped the order and praised him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 家令薛居敬上言陝西分地五事，因被命往理之，約不為署行，語之曰：「太子，潛龍也。

translations.literal: Household Director Xue Jujing memorialized on five matters of land division in Shaanxi and was therefore ordered to go settle them; Yue would not sign the travel authorization and told him: "The Crown Prince is a hidden dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Household Director Xue Jujing memorialized on five Shaanxi land disputes and was ordered to settle them; Yue refused to authorize the mission and said, "The crown prince is a hidden dragon.

sentences.zh: 當勿用之時，為飛龍之事可乎？」

translations.literal: When he should not yet be employed, can one do the deeds of a soaring dragon?"
translations.idiomatic: Before his time has come, can he do the deeds of a soaring dragon?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The mission was halted.

sentences.zh: 薦翰林學士李謙為太子少傅，請立故丞相淮安忠武王伯顏祠於杭，皆從之。

translations.literal: He recommended Hanlin Academician Li Qian as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and requested establishing a shrine at Hangzhou to the former Chancellor, Loyal and Martial King of Huai'an, Bayan—all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Hanlin academician Li Qian as junior tutor to the heir and petitioned for a shrine to the former chancellor Bayan, Loyal and Martial King of Huai'an, at Hangzhou—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以詹事院諸事循軌，大喜，面賜犀帶，力辭；

translations.literal: Because all affairs of the Heir Apparent's Household followed proper course, Renzong was greatly pleased and in person bestowed a rhinoceros-horn belt; Yue strenuously declined;
translations.idiomatic: Renzong was delighted that the heir's household ran properly, personally gave him a rhinoceros-horn belt, which Yue firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 又賜江南所取書籍，亦辭。

translations.literal: books taken from Jiangnan were again granted, and he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: he also declined books brought from Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 仁宗常字而不名，諭群臣曰：「事未經王彥博議者，勿啟。」

translations.literal: Renzong often used his style and not his name, instructing the ministers: "Matters that have not passed through Wang Yanbo's deliberation—do not bring them forward."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong often called him by his style rather than his name and told the ministers, "Do not bring forward any matter that Wang Yanbo has not reviewed."

sentences.zh: 又謂中丞朵䚟曰：「在詹事而不求賜予者，惟彥博與汝二人耳。」

translations.literal: He also said to Censor-in-Chief Duo Na: "Among those in the Heir Apparent's office who do not seek gifts, only Yanbo and you are such."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Censor-in-Chief Duo Na, "Of those in the heir's office who seek no gifts, only Yanbo and you are such."

sentences.zh: 一日，仁宗西園觀角抵戲，有旨取繒帛賜之。

translations.literal: One day Renzong watched wrestling in the Western Garden; an edict ordered silk fabrics taken to bestow on the performers.
translations.idiomatic: One day Renzong watched wrestling in the Western Garden and ordered silks for the performers.

sentences.zh: 約入，遙見問曰：「汝何為來？」

translations.literal: Yue entered; seeing him from afar Renzong asked: "Why have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yue entered, Renzong saw him from afar and asked, "Why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗遽止之。

translations.literal: Renzong at once stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong stopped him at once.

sentences.zh: 又欲觀俳戲，事已集而約至，即命罷去，其見敬禮如此。

translations.literal: He again wished to watch comic plays; the affair was already assembled when Yue arrived, and he at once ordered it dismissed—such was the respect and courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: When he wished to watch comic plays and Yue arrived just as they were ready, he ordered them dismissed at once—such was the respect he showed him.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，仁宗正位宸極，欲用陰陽家言，即位光天殿，即東宮也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year Renzong took the imperial throne; wishing to follow the yin-yang masters' words, he would ascend at the Hall of Radiant Heaven, which was the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 4 Renzong took the throne; following geomancers' advice he meant to be enthroned in the Hall of Radiant Heaven, which was the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 約言於太保曲樞曰：「正名定分，當禦大內。」

translations.literal: Yue spoke to Grand Guardian Qu Shu: "To rectify names and fix ranks, one should mount the throne in the Great Inner Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Yue told Grand Guardian Qu Shu, "To set names and ranks aright, the enthronement should be in the Great Inner Palace."

sentences.zh: 太保入奏，遂即位於大明殿。

translations.literal: The Grand Guardian entered to memorialize, and the enthronement was then carried out at the Hall of Great Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Shu reported this, and the enthronement was held in the Hall of Great Brightness.

sentences.zh: 中書奏約陝西行省參知政事，帝大怒，特拜河南行省右丞。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat memorialized appointing Yue Vice Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; the Emperor was greatly angry and specially appointed him Right Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat proposed him as vice administrator of Shaanxi, the emperor was angry and instead specially appointed him right chancellor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 約陛辭，帝賜卮酒及弓矢。

translations.literal: Yue took leave at the steps; the Emperor granted a goblet of wine, bow, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: As Yue took leave, the emperor gave him wine, a bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 先是，至大間尚書省用建言者，冒獻河、汴官民地為無主，奏立田糧府，歲輸數万石，是歲詔罷之，竄建言人於海外，命河南行省复其舊業。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Zhida period the Ministry of Revenue had used a memorialist who falsely presented official and private lands of the Yellow River and Bian regions as ownerless, memorialized to establish a Field-Tax Office, and yearly delivered tens of thousands of shi; that year an edict abolished it, banished the memorialist overseas, and ordered the Henan Branch Secretariat to restore the people's former holdings.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhida reign the Ministry of Revenue had used a memorialist who falsely declared Yellow River and Bian lands ownerless, set up a field-tax office yielding tens of thousands of shi yearly; that year the office was abolished, the memorialist banished overseas, and Henan was ordered to restore the original holdings.

sentences.zh: 行省方並緣為奸，田猶未給。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat was just then taking advantage to practice corruption, and the fields had still not been returned.
translations.idiomatic: The regional secretariat was still corruptly obstructing return of the land.

sentences.zh: 約至，立期檄郡縣，厘正如詔。

translations.literal: When Yue arrived he set a deadline and sent orders to prefectures and counties; restoration followed the edict exactly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue arrived he set deadlines and ordered the prefectures and counties to restore holdings exactly as the edict required.

sentences.zh: 會詔更銅錢銀鈔法，且令天下稅，盡收至大鈔。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict revised the regulations for copper cash and silver notes, and moreover ordered taxes throughout the empire collected entirely in Zhida notes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then revised copper cash and paper currency and ordered all taxes collected in Zhida notes.

sentences.zh: 約度河南歲用鈔七萬錠，必致上供不給，乃下諸州，凡至大、至元鈔相半。

translations.literal: Yue estimated Henan's yearly use of notes at seventy thousand ingots and that this would necessarily cause tribute to the center to fall short; he therefore issued orders to the prefectures that Zhida and Zhiyuan notes should each be half.
translations.idiomatic: Yue calculated that Henan needed seventy thousand ingots yearly and that full Zhida collection would leave tribute short; he ordered the prefectures to accept Zhida and Zhiyuan notes in equal halves.

sentences.zh: 眾以方詔命為言，約曰：「吾豈不知，第歲終諸事不集，責亦匪輕。」

translations.literal: The crowd spoke of the recent edict; Yue said: "Do I not know that? But if at year's end affairs are not gathered, the blame is also not light."
translations.idiomatic: When others cited the recent edict, Yue said, "I know—but if year-end targets are not met, the blame will be heavy."

sentences.zh: 丞相卜憐吉台讚之曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Bulqinjang praised it, saying: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bulqinjang praised him, saying, "Well done."

sentences.zh: 遣使白中書，省臣大悅，遂遍行天下。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to inform the Central Secretariat; the provincial ministers were greatly pleased, and it was then implemented throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the Secretariat; the ministers were delighted, and the policy was adopted empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 南陽孛術魯衝以書謁約，大奇之，即署為郡學正。

translations.literal: Nanyang's Beshbaluq Chong presented a letter calling on Yue; Yue greatly marveled at him and at once appointed him Rectifier of the Prefectural School.
translations.idiomatic: Beshbaluq Chong of Nanyang presented a letter to Yue, who was greatly impressed and appointed him rectifier of the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 既又薦之中書，擢翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Later he again recommended him to the Central Secretariat, and he was promoted to Compiler of the Hanlin National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He later recommended him to the Secretariat, and Chong was made compiler in the Hanlin National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 皇慶改元元日，詔中書省曰：「汴省王右丞可即召之。」

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the Huangqing reign change, an edict to the Central Secretariat said: "The Right Chancellor Wang of Bian may be summoned at once."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the Huangqing era change, an edict to the Secretariat said, "Summon Right Chancellor Wang of Bian at once."

sentences.zh: 約以三月一日至，召見，慰勞，特拜集賢大學士，推恩三世，贈諡樹碑。

translations.literal: Yue arrived on the first day of the third month, was summoned to audience, consoled and commended, specially appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, with grace extended three generations, posthumous titles and steles erected.
translations.idiomatic: Yue arrived on the first day of the third month, was received and commended, specially made Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, with honors extended three generations and posthumous titles and steles granted.

sentences.zh: 約首奏：「河南行省丞相卜憐吉台，勳閥舊臣，不宜久外。」

translations.literal: Yue's first memorial said: "Chancellor Bulqinjang of the Henan Branch Secretariat, an old minister of meritorious lineage, should not long remain abroad."
translations.idiomatic: Yue's first memorial said, "Chancellor Bulqinjang of Henan, a veteran of meritorious lineage, should not long remain in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 召至，封河南王。

translations.literal: He was summoned and enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 約又建議行封贈、禁服色、興科舉。

translations.literal: Yue again proposed implementing posthumous enfeoffment and gifts, prohibiting certain garment colors, and reviving the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also proposed reviving posthumous honors, restricting garment colors, and restoring the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 皆著為令甲。

translations.literal: All were written as binding ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: All were enacted as binding statutes.

sentences.zh: 上疏薦國子博士姚登孫、應奉翰林文字揭傒斯、成都儒士楊靜，請起復中山知府致仕輔惟良、前尚書參議李源、左司員外郎曹元用，皆除擢有差。

translations.literal: He memorialized recommending National University Doctor Yao Dengsun, Hanlin Attendant Document Drafter Jie Xisi, and Chengdu scholar Yang Jing; requesting restoration of retired Zhongshan Prefect Fu Weiliang, former Ministry of Revenue Participating Secretary Li Yuan, and Left Department Vice Director Cao Yuanyong—all were appointed and promoted with distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended National University doctor Yao Dengsun, Hanlin attendant document drafter Jie Xisi, and Chengdu scholar Yang Jing; he also asked to recall retired Zhongshan prefect Fu Weiliang, former participating secretary Li Yuan, and left department vice director Cao Yuanyong—all were appointed in due rank.

sentences.zh: 辯奏故左丞竇履有遺腹子棄外，宜收養歸宗，為竇氏後。

translations.literal: He argued in memorial that the former Left Chancellor Dou Lü had a posthumous son cast out, who ought to be taken in and restored to the clan as heir to the Dou line.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that former Left Chancellor Dou Lü's posthumous son, cast out, should be taken in and restored as heir to the Dou line.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，丞相帖木迭兒專政，奏遣大臣分道奉使宣撫，命約巡行燕南山東道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou, Chancellor Temür dominated government and memorialized dispatching great ministers in separate routes as pacification envoys; Yue was ordered to tour the Yan-South and Shandong circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 (1315), when Chancellor Temür dominated the government, great ministers were sent as pacification envoys on separate routes; Yue was ordered to tour Yan-South and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 約至衛輝，有毆母置獄者，其母泣訴，言老妾惟此一息，死則一門絕矣。

translations.literal: When Yue reached Weihui there was one imprisoned for beating his mother; the mother wept and appealed, saying this old woman has only this one son—if he dies the whole house is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: At Weihui a man was imprisoned for beating his mother; she wept and pleaded that she had only this one son and the family line would end if he died.

sentences.zh: 約原其情，杖一百而遣之。

translations.literal: Yue excused him according to circumstance, caned him one hundred strokes, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Yue showed mercy, gave him a hundred strokes, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 冠州民有兄訐其弟厭詛者，讞之，則曰：「我求嗣也。」

translations.literal: In Guan Prefecture a man had an elder brother who accused his younger brother of cursing with malicious intent; on judgment the younger said: "I was seeking an heir."
translations.idiomatic: In Guan Prefecture an elder brother accused his younger brother of casting a curse; when questioned the younger said, "I was seeking an heir."

sentences.zh: 索《授時曆》驗其日良信，乃立縱之使還。

translations.literal: He sought the Season-Granting Calendar to verify the day—it was truly so—and at once released him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the Season-Granting Calendar and found the date correct, then released him at once.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密副使，視事，明日召見賜酒，帝謂左右曰：「人言彥博老病，朕今見之，精力尚強，可堪大任也。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and assumed duties; the next day he was summoned to audience and granted wine; the Emperor said to those beside him: "People say Yanbo is old and ill—today I have seen him; his vigor is still strong and he can bear great responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he took office; summoned the next day and given wine, the emperor told his attendants, "People say Yanbo is old and ill, but I see his vigor is still strong and he can bear great responsibility."

sentences.zh: 是夕，知院駙馬塔失帖木兒宿衛，帝戒之曰：「彥博非汝友，宜師事之。」

translations.literal: That evening Court Director and Imperial Son-in-Law Tas Temür was on night guard; the Emperor admonished him: "Yanbo is not your friend—you ought to take him as teacher."
translations.idiomatic: That evening Court Director and imperial son-in-law Tas Temür was on night guard; the emperor warned him, "Yanbo is not your friend—you should treat him as your teacher."

sentences.zh: 至治元年，英宗即位，帖木迭兒復相，約辭職不出。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Emperor Yingzong took the throne; Temür again became chancellor; Yue resigned and did not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1 (1321), when Emperor Yingzong acceded, Temür returned as chancellor; Yue resigned and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 二年，以年七十致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year, at age seventy he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, at seventy, he retired.

sentences.zh: 三年，丞相拜住一新政務，尊禮老臣，傳詔起約，復拜集賢大學士，商議中書省事，以其祿居家，每日一至中書省議事，至治之政，多所參酌。

translations.literal: In the third year Chancellor Bayiju undertook a new administration, honored old ministers, and by transmitted edict raised Yue; he was again appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs, living at home on his salary, coming once each day to the Central Secretariat to deliberate on affairs; Zhizhi policies were largely shaped by his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Chancellor Bayiju reformed the government, honored veteran ministers, and recalled Yue as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to advise on Secretariat affairs; living at home on his salary, he came daily to deliberate, and Zhizhi policy owed much to him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗奉詔與中書省官及他舊臣，條定國初以來律令，名曰《大元通制》，頒行天下。

translations.literal: He also once received an edict, together with Central Secretariat officials and other old ministers, to itemize and fix laws and ordinances from the founding of the state onward, entitled Comprehensive Regulations of the Great Yuan, and promulgate them throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped codify laws since the founding of the dynasty into the Comprehensive Regulations of the Great Yuan, promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議罷征東省，立三韓省，制式如他省，詔下中書雜議，約對曰：「高麗去京師四千里，地瘠民貧，夷俗雜尚，非中原比，萬一梗化，疲力治之，非幸事也，不如守祖宗舊制。」
